short: Revolutionary English Romantic painter renowned for his expressive, atmospheric landscapes and seascapes.
full:
Joseph Mallord William Turner was a prodigious artistic talent who entered the Royal Academy of Arts at fourteen and quickly established himself as a master of both watercolour and oil painting. Initially rooted in the classical landscape tradition, his work grew increasingly radical over his long career, prioritising the emotional impact of colour and light over precise topographical detail.

His later masterpieces, such as The Fighting Temeraire and Rain, Steam and Speed, captured the visceral energy of the natural world and the profound disruptions of the Industrial Revolution. By dissolving physical forms into swirling vortexes of luminous colour, Turner laid the conceptual groundwork for the Impressionist movement that would follow decades later.
